blocks.heading: A shop you can walk around
blocks.body:
We sell things we would happily own ourselves: mugs from a potter down the road, honey from a hive behind the library, notebooks sewn by hand.

We do not run an online shop. The best way to buy is to visit. If you cannot, send an enquiry about anything you spot here and we will set it aside, or post it to you.

blocks.heading: What is on the shelves
blocks.body:
Prices are what you will pay in the shop, and stock changes week to week. To ask about something, send an enquiry or give us a ring and we will put it aside.

**No online checkout.** Visit us, or send an enquiry and we will reply with how to collect or post it.

pages.title: Gift cards
pages.description: Ask the shop for a hand-written gift card.

blocks.heading: A little something, for someone.
blocks.subheading: Gift cards are written by hand, for any amount from $10. Ask below and collect it in the shop, or have it posted.
blocks.alt: A terracotta gift card tied up with a note that reads: a little something, for someone

blocks.heading: How it works
blocks.body:
1. Fill in the form below with who it is for and how much.
2. We write the card and get in touch to arrange payment in the shop or by phone.
3. You collect it, or we post it for the price of a stamp.

Cards do not expire, and they can be spent on anything in the shop.

pages.title: Our story
pages.description: How a spare room of jars became a shop.

blocks.heading: From a spare room to a high street
blocks.body:
Bea started with a table at the village fair and a box of jam jars. People kept asking where the rest of it came from, so she began to buy from the people who made it: the potter, the knitters, the beekeeper behind the library.

Walter joined to help with the lifting and stayed for the tea. The shop opened on a rainy Tuesday and has been open on most Tuesdays since.

items.question: Is the shop step-free?
items.answer: Yes. There is a ramp at the door and the aisles are wide enough for a pushchair or a wheelchair.

items.question: Can I bring my dog?
items.answer: Well-behaved dogs are very welcome. There is a water bowl by the till.

items.question: Do you take cards?
items.answer: Yes, and cash, and the occasional jar of honey in exchange.

items.question: Can I buy online?
items.answer: No. We deliberately have no online checkout. Send an enquiry and we will set things aside or post them.
